analysis.title: Ruminations Macro Micro Markets: Feast and then famine
key_insights: Last 2-3 weeks were hard to trade. The index level held high while sector, factor, spread and theme volatility was large. Anyone carrying gross lost money across regions and strategies.
Nasdaq is down over 6% in two weeks, with a semiconductor rout. Momentum is down about 15% over the same period. Credit instruments linked to the AI buildout moved sharply.
The GS risk indicator has fallen sharply over 3 weeks and is negative for the first time since March. Investors are waiting for a bottom to become evident rather than calling one.

Private equity reports on the size of AI financing and mark-to-market on returns, plus a strategist report showing revenue per worker and profit margins up for the Mag 7 but flat for the S&P 493, are shifting corporate focus from token spend tied to growth toward token spend as a cost to margins.

Oil is moving back toward its April/May highs on Middle East anxiety. Civil unrest in France has pushed OAT-Bund spreads to record highs. Falling yields are no longer welcomed because they are tied to the AI unwind and possible capex slowing.
Key anchors remain AI, oil and yields, with credit and credit spreads added. Investors are rotating to defensive, real assets, quality and low leverage names while de-grossing and playing defense.

This week's data covers the Middle East (before the midterms), whether yields are normalising, and whether Friday's AI reversal started a rebound or a deeper sell-off. Meta news this morning could be a clearing event.

A large share of the S&P reports this week. Results so far have been solid with little reward. Three hyperscalers will give more detail on capex and ROI. Meta raising capex and Tesla cutting capex both sold off.
H1 treated all news as good. H2 sets a higher bar for good news and treats most news as bad. Fed hike probability has dropped from near certainty to about 75% over the last couple of weeks.

Seasonal: in 30 years the S&P has had only 3 November drawdowns (2000 -8%, 2007 -4.4%, 2008 -7.48%), each in a broader drawdown year. Other Novembers were flat or materially up. A red November has tended to precede much larger declines.

Token demand on OpenRouter is up 27x since last November, with open-weight models at 72% of tokens. GPU rental prices are up YTD: H200 +160%, B200 +120%, H100 +35%, and even the A100 rents for more than at the start of the year. Bulls and bears both cite this data.

S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average rose 5 points Friday to 61%, the highest since August, and the measure is up 17 points in three weeks while the S&P is roughly unchanged. The unwind has cleared positioning, reduced concentration and normalised multiples.

Private-market exits are headline-large but concentrated and interdependent (SpaceX, Cerebras, Cursor, Hugging Face). Venture funds are crowding in and valuations are rising on little more than term sheets. This diverges from public markets, which are in an AI risk-off. Re-rating through IPOs can be bumpy (Firmus, Oura).

Boom loops: hyperscaler capex drives AI-ecosystem revenue, which pulls in venture and growth capital. Sustainability without the capex anchor is the missing link. Vendor financing blurs revenue and financing lines.
Market narratives have shifted from COVID-era stories to cash flow focus in 2022 to AI disruption and the demand for chips, cloud, compute and power.

tension_points.bull_case: Token demand is up 27x and GPU rental prices are up (H200 +160% YTD), so demand is broadening and the addressable market is growing.
tension_points.bear_case: Cost per token versus revenue per token is moving the wrong way as power shifts to open-weight models, and productivity gains are not yet visible outside tech.

tension_points.bull_case: Friday's AI reversion was the start of a rebound, with the Meta news a possible clearing event.
tension_points.bear_case: It was an uptick inside a deeper, broader sell-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A red November, which has historically signalled larger declines.
